# SB-1032 Safety bulletin: hot metal and scale ejection
Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-SB02

Hazard description
This bulletin addresses the hazard of hot metal and scale ejection from the shot blast cabinet in the hot forge area. During normal operation, workpieces that retain adhered hot material or heavy scale can dislodge under shot media impact and be expelled from the cabinet aperture or access points. Ejected fragments pose burn and impact hazards to operators, support personnel, and nearby process lines, and can damage adjacent equipment, fixtures, and controls. Scale dust generated during ejection events can create additional inhalation and slip hazards in the immediate work area and on travel paths used by personnel and material handlers.

Background and rationale
The hot forge environment produces workpieces with variable surface condition; significant adherent material or scale can change how a workpiece responds to shot blasting. When adhered material separates under kinetic loading, it can behave unpredictably, including sideways projection or rebound trajectories that follow shot media flow patterns. Containment breaches commonly involve worn or improperly secured access seals, misaligned doors, or temporary openings used to expedite part loading. The top-up and conditioning of shot media affect blast patterns and containment; irregular media distribution can concentrate impact on workpiece features that promote ejection.

This bulletin is issued in response to recurring near-miss reports and observations of small projectiles exiting access points during blasting cycles. It is intended to clarify controls and administrative steps to reduce the probability of ejection and to ensure appropriate documentation and corrective follow-up when events occur. See related guidance in SB-1027 for general blast area risk management and in SOP-P3-L1-01 and SOP-P3-L1-05 for operator procedures and maintenance tasks.

Affected equipment
This bulletin applies to Hot Forge shot blast cabinet number identified as EQ-P3-L1-SB02 on line P3-L1 in plant P3. Also included are immediate support structures such as cabinet doors, access seals, observation windows, local exhaust interfaces, loading fixtures and any temporary barriers used during loading or maintenance activities in the same work cell. Operators, maintenance technicians, and supervisors assigned to EQ-P3-L1-SB02 or to adjacent process steps that could be exposed to expelled material are in scope for the controls below.

Required controls
Engineering controls
- Ensure all cabinet access panels and observation ports are secured with factory fittings and maintained in the closed configuration during blasting. Replace or repair any worn or misfitting seals before returning the cabinet to service.
- Maintain containment skirts, deflectors, and internal shields in accordance with manufacturer layout. Where local deflectors have been removed for tooling changes, a written temporary alteration must be approved by the shift supervisor and maintenance lead prior to operation; restore original configuration when the alteration is complete.
- Verify that the loading fixture orientation and part clamping prevent unconstrained movement during blasting. Use fixtures that minimize exposed surfaces that can act as leverage points for scale or loose material to be thrown outward.

Administrative controls
- Implement pre-blast inspection checklists that include visual confirmation of seal integrity, door latches, fixture security, and the absence of loose material in the feed area.
- The shot media top-up interval for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is 45 hours. Record each top-up action in the cabinet media log and attach the operator initials and cabinet condition remarks at the time of top-up.
- Require that any operation involving parts with visible heavy scale or with known adherence issues be evaluated at staging prior to transfer to the cabinet. Where risk of ejection is assessed as unacceptable, parts must be pre-cleaned or descaled at the pre-processing station and re-evaluated before blasting.
- Enforce a prohibition on bypassing interlocks, removing guards during cycle initiation, or holding open observation panels while blasting is in progress. Any temporary override must be documented and approved as an exception with compensating controls in place.

Personal protective equipment and access control
- Restrict access to the immediate blast area to assigned personnel only during blasting operations. Position warning signage at the blast cabinet perimeter and maintain a safe zone during active cycles.
- Require appropriate PPE for personnel in the work cell, consistent with hot metal exposure and particulate risks identified in SB-1027. Supervisors must verify compliance at shift start and record verification in the shift safety log.

Examples and implementation notes
- Example scenario: A heavily scaled flange is placed in the cabinet without pre-cleaning. During blasting, a large piece of scale dislodges and is projected through a misaligned observation port. Under these controls, the part would be staged for pre-clean, the port alignment would be checked in the pre-blast checklist, and the event would be prevented.
- Example documentation flow: Operator completes pre-blast checklist, supervisor reviews and initials, shot media top-up is logged as required, and maintenance closes any noted deficiencies before the next cycle begins.

Records to keep
- Maintain the cabinet media log for EQ-P3-L1-SB02 that records each top-up action and operator initials. The entry must include the cabinet condition remarks recorded at the time of top-up.
- Retain pre-blast inspection checklists and any temporary alteration approvals in the local cabinet file and attach them to the daily equipment ledger. Documented approvals for any operation involving parts with heavy scale must be kept with the work order for that production run.
- Record any ejection incidents with a description of the sequence, immediate corrective actions taken, root cause analysis outcome, and verification of corrective actions. Reference SB-1027 for incident classification and reporting thresholds and use SOP-P3-L1-01 and SOP-P3-L1-05 for procedural steps to follow during response and maintenance.

Effective date
Effective date: immediate. All supervisors and equipment custodians for EQ-P3-L1-SB02 must ensure that the controls in this bulletin are implemented in their areas without delay and that staff are briefed on the changes. Review compliance during the next scheduled safety audit and escalate unresolved deficiencies through the P3 safety chain of command.
